Accepted.description: The one answer sign-up, resend and forgot-password give, whatever the address.
Accepted.title: Accepted

AdminUserPatch.description: Only the fields present are changed. `hours_cap_seconds: null` clears the override.
AdminUserPatch.title: AdminUserPatch

info.description:
Owner-only JSON API for the Beyric Note Taker frontend. Same origin as the app.

Auth is the signed `session` cookie. Call `GET /api/session` first: it returns `csrf_token`,
which every call other than GET must send in the `X-CSRF-Token` header. Every error has the
shape `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` (validation errors add `fields`).
info.title: Beyric Note Taker API

get.description: The most recent mail that could not be sent (never with its link).

put.description:
Open or close sign-up, set the number of accounts (`null` = no limit), the default recorded
hours per account in seconds (`null` = no cap) and whether password sign-up is on. Every field
is required.

get.description: Accounts with their recorded hours, newest first. Accounts being deleted are not listed.

delete.description:
Delete an account and everything of theirs. The user is signed out and their slot is free
at once; the worker then removes their data (bots stopped, recordings deleted at Vexa and
here). The hours ledger keeps seconds only. 409 `last_admin`.

patch.description:
Suspend or reactivate an account (`status`) and set or clear one user's hours override
(`hours_cap_seconds`). Only the fields sent change. A suspended user is signed out on their
next request. 409 `last_admin`: the only active admin cannot be suspended.

post.description:
A one-time password-reset link (30 minutes) for the admin to give the person, for when
mail is not working. Shown once, never mailed; replaces any earlier reset link and tells the
user in the app. Not for admin accounts. 409 `admin_account`, `user_not_verified` or
`account_suspended`.

get.description:
The waiting list, oldest first, without the people removed. `before_id` is the id to
continue after (the last `next_before_id`).

delete.description: Take someone off the list. A live invitation is cancelled and its place freed.

post.description:
Reserve a place for this person for 7 days and invite them. With mail working the link
is emailed (`emailed: true`, `invite_url: null`); without it `invite_url` is returned for the
admin to send. Inviting again replaces the earlier link. 409 `pilot_full` when no place is
free, `waitlist_entry_closed` for someone who joined or was removed.

get.description:
Where Google sends the browser back. Public (checked by the single-use `state` and the
`google_flow` cookie of the browser that started the flow). Always a redirect, never JSON:
success goes to the stored `return_to` with a new session; a failure goes to
`/login?error=<code>` with `google_denied`, `google_failed`, `terms_required`,
`account_suspended`, `pilot_closed` or `email_unsupported`; a full pilot goes to
`/pilot-full` and sets a 15-minute cookie that `GET /api/pilot` reads as `prefill_email`
(the address is never put in a URL).

Send the browser to Google's consent screen (scopes `openid email profile` only). Public;
navigate to it, do not fetch it. `accept_terms=true` must be sent by the sign-up screen: it
is what lets a NEW account be created (an existing one signs in without it). `return_to` is
a relative path to land on afterwards; anything else becomes `/`. 404
`google_signin_unavailable` when the server has no Google client configured.

The caller's meetings, newest first. For the next page pass `before_id` =
`next_before_id`.

post.description:
Send the bot to a Google Meet or Zoom link. One bot at a time: 409 while one is active.
403 `hours_cap_reached` once the account has used its recorded hours.

Take the bot out of a meeting that is still `bot_sent` and discard it. Only when `can_cancel`
is true: once the bot has been ended with `POST /end` (the notes are being written) it is 409
`already_ending`; 409 `meeting_busy` when the worker holds the meeting, try again.

"End now and write the notes": take the bot out of the call and write the notes from what
it recorded. Only when `can_end` is true (409 `not_endable` otherwise, 409 `already_ending`
when it was asked already, 409 `meeting_busy` when the worker holds the meeting: try again).
The meeting stays `bot_sent` while the bot leaves, then follows the usual steps; it is not a
cancel and nothing is discarded.
Rewrite the notes of a `ready` meeting with a template. Runs in the request: allow 5 min.

Resume a failed meeting at the step that failed. Only when `can_retry` is true. For a
meeting whose join the worker ended (Google refused the bot, or it hung on a prompt) this
sends a new bot instead, no sooner than 5 minutes after the failure.

get.description:
The caller's notifications, newest first. For the next page pass `before_id` =
`next_before_id`.

post.description: Mark all of the caller's notifications read.

Mark one notification read (repeating it keeps the first read time). 404 for someone
else's.

Mail a password-reset link (valid 30 minutes) if the address has a confirmed account.
Public. Always 202 with the same body: it never says whether the address has an account.

Choose a new password with the token from the reset mail. Public. Signs that user out
everywhere and does not sign them in. 400 `token_invalid_or_expired`; 422
`password_too_weak` leaves the token usable.

get.description:
Whether sign-up is `open`, `full` or `closed`. Public. No counts of other people.

`prefill_email` is the Google address of a visitor just turned away by `pilot_full` (a signed
15-minute cookie), so the waitlist form can start filled in. `google_signin` says whether the
Google button should be shown.

delete.description:
Log this user out everywhere: every session cookie they were issued stops working.
Other users are not affected.

get.description:
Whether the cookie is a logged-in session, plus the CSRF token to send on writes.

Public. Call it first: it also gives a logged-out visitor a cookie to log in with. Logged in,
it names the user and reports their recorded hours (`usage`).

post.description:
Log in with email and password. Public, but needs the X-CSRF-Token from `GET /session`.

401 `invalid_credentials` for a wrong password or an unknown email (the same answer for
both, and for an account whose email was never confirmed). 403 `account_suspended` when the
password was right but the account is suspended. The login limits are the page's: 5 failed
attempts per client address in 5 minutes and 10 per email in an hour, then 429. The response
carries the new session's CSRF token: it replaces the one from before login.

Create an account with a password. Public (needs the X-CSRF-Token).

Answers 202 `check_your_email` for a new address AND for one that already has an account (a
verified one gets a "you already have an account" mail), so it cannot be used to find out who
is registered. The account cannot sign in until the emailed link is confirmed. Errors that do
not depend on the address: 403 `pilot_closed`, 409 `pilot_full`, 403
`password_signup_disabled`, 400 `invite_invalid`, 422 `password_too_weak`, `invalid_email`,
`invalid_name`, `terms_required`, 429 `too_many_requests` (5 sign-ups per hour per address)
and `server_busy`. `accept_terms` must be true: the account records the version accepted.
A second sign-up for the same address within a minute is answered 202 and does nothing.

Mail a new verification link to an unconfirmed account. Public. Always 202, whatever the
address and whether or not a mail was sent: one per minute per email and 5 per hour per
client address are sent, the rest are dropped silently.

get.description: The caller's templates, sorted by name.

post.description:
Confirm an email with the token from the link and the password chosen at sign-up.
Public. The page the link opens must show a password field and a button that calls this
(mail scanners open links, and a GET must not verify). Does not sign the user in.
400 `token_invalid_or_expired`: wrong, used or older than 24 hours. 400 `password_mismatch`:
not the password submitted with this link's sign-up; the link stays usable until 5 wrong
passwords, after which it answers `token_invalid_or_expired`.

Leave an email (and optionally a name) for when a place opens. Public. Always 202
`on_the_list`, whether or not the address is already listed or has an account; a repeat
changes nothing, and 5 per hour per address and 1 per minute per email are dropped silently.
422 `invalid_email` for a malformed address.
